nodes.label: OpenClaw Incident (Feb 2026)
nodes.rationale: A trading agent built on OpenClaw misread a user's request for 4 SOL and transferred its entire holdings (~$250,000), dumped within 15 minutes. No hack, no exploit. The agent simply misunderstood. Proves hallucination doesn't need an attacker.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Attack
nodes.rationale: AI agents that read external content have no architectural boundary between data and commands. The only sensible defense is containment: bounding the blast radius of a hijacked agent within the human-approved mandate.

nodes.label: Refusal Stamp Component
nodes.rationale: The authored moment of the entire system. An inline-flex block with a 3px refusal-red border, rotated -8 degrees, carrying the contract's own error name. The stamp is split into .stamp (rendered evidence, always server-side) and .stamp-in (entrance animation, added by JS). Evidence never animates in.

nodes.label: The Refusal is the Hero
nodes.rationale: Every payments dashboard celebrates successes. Leash's entire value is what it refuses. A green checkmark proves nothing; a revert proves the firewall works. The attack results get the largest, most designed surface on the page.

nodes.label: Stamped Ledger Design Concept
nodes.rationale: Leash's web surface is a paper document that happens to be live. The refusal stamp is the single loudest element; approval is deliberately quiet. The imbalance is the design: a green result proves nothing, a revert proves the firewall works.

nodes.label: Model B: Authority on Chain
nodes.rationale: Blockchain used as enforcement layer for spending authority while money stays in fiat rails. Backend remains trusted to follow protocol, but deviations are auditable. Not full trustlessness but more than status quo.

nodes.label: Agent is Untrusted by Design
nodes.rationale: The agent is expected to be wrong, manipulated, or compromised. Hardening the agent rather than the boundary would defend at the wrong layer. A successful prompt injection that the contract rejects is the demonstration, not a bug.

nodes.label: Authorization vs Settlement Boundary
nodes.rationale: AuthorizationGranted means the request satisfied the on-chain mandate at a particular block. It does not mean money moved. The two are never conflated in code, copy, or interface.

nodes.label: Claim Only What Is Verified
nodes.rationale: Mocked components are named as mocked, unbuilt things stay unclaimed, and the gap between proven and production-ready is stated rather than blurred.

nodes.label: Contract is the Only Gate
nodes.rationale: Enforcement never moves off-chain for convenience. Any client-side check that duplicates the contract's logic conceals whether the real gate works. The frontend and agent are clients of the contract, never reimplementers of enforcement.

nodes.label: Fiat Stays Off-Chain
nodes.rationale: Fiat settlement depends on licensed banking partners, card networks, custody, KYC, AML, disputes, refunds, and jurisdiction-specific compliance. Putting those operations into this MVP would obscure the core authorization proof.

nodes.label: No Client-Side Policy Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Policy enforcement happens on-chain only. No client-side allowlist, cap, or expiry check anywhere in the frontend or the agent's tools. Duplicating the gate off-chain would relocate trust to the exact layer the product argues against.
